title: Council of the European Union, general approach on extending the CBAM to downstream goods, document ST 10423/2026, 12 June 2026
snippet: Primary document, listed as a PDF and therefore not opened here. The article cites it by number and date for the one fact it carries: the Council reached a general approach on 12 June 2026, which is a negotiating position and not adopted law. Recorded as cited-but-not-read, because the article's claim about the Council's position rests on the document's existence and date rather than on its text.

title: European Parliament, plenary document A-10-2026-0201, committee report on the amending proposal
snippet: Primary document, a PDF, not opened here. Its existence establishes that the amending proposal is before the European Parliament, which is what the article says about the trilogue stage. No provision is quoted from it.

title: European Parliament written question P-002207/2026, answer given by Mr Hoekstra on behalf of the Commission, 21 August 2026
snippet: Attempted and the request returned an unreadable PDF. Recorded as attempted-and-not-read. This would have been the strongest available check on how the Commission itself characterises the downstream extension; because it could not be read, the article quotes no Commission statement about the extension.

title: CBAM Weekly, The Council Agrees on CBAM Extension: Downstream Steel and Aluminum Products Will Be Included in the Scope in 2028
snippet: Read in full, and it is trade-compliance analysis rather than a primary source. It is the origin of the operational detail: the ex-code mechanism capturing only the steel or aluminium content of a good, the requirement to report material composition, the two-step extension of Annex I including a new combined-metal-goods table, the 1 January 2028 application date, and pre-consumer scrap becoming a precursor with emissions. No per-unit cost table and no figure for what the charge would be on any named product.

title: CBAM product scope analysis: current sectors and the downstream expansion path
snippet: Read in full. A Chinese-language secondary account, dated September 2026. It states that a Commission proposal in December 2025 would bring approximately 180 downstream steel- and aluminium-intensive products into scope from 1 January 2028, and that about 94 per cent of them are industrial supply-chain goods with the remaining 6 per cent household appliances. No per-tonne or per-unit cost figure anywhere in it; the article cites the 180 figure with attribution and does not treat it as settled because it was not read from the legislative text.

title: CBAM Downstream Extension: 180 Goods in 2028
snippet: Reached, and the body was truncated on retrieval so only the title and framing were obtained. Recorded as reached-but-unread. Its title corroborates the 180-goods figure independently of the Chinese account, which is why the article reports the number with attribution rather than as a fact read from the annexes.
